newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Amplats plans new S.African platinum mine.
newsitem.headline: Amplats plans new S.African platinum mine.

text.p: Anglo American Platinum Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Tuesday it planned to develop a new platinum mine at Boschkoppie in the Rustenburg area of South Africa and would also expand concentrator capacity at Potgietersrust Platinums Ltd.
Annual platinum output from Boschkoppie was expected to be about 250,000 ounces of refined platinum metal when full production is reached in 2002, the company said in a statement.
Amplats said the new projects would increase operational flexibility and cut costs.
"The group will be better placed to take advantage of a platinum supply deficit forecast to appear in the medium term," it added.
Amplats said the Boschkoppie reserve represented what is believed to be the last remaining source of viable Merensky Reef outcrop in the Western Bushveld Complex.
Over the life of the project some 60 million tonnes of ore are expected to be mined at an estimated head grade of 6.1 grams per tonne of platinum, palladium, rhodium and gold.

The Boschkoppie reserve will be exploited through two sets of twin incline shafts with a combined hoisting capacity of 200,000 tonnes a month. Production is anticipated to commence in 2000. The life of the mine is expected to be at least 25 years.
Capital expenditure on the new mine, including building a concentrator, is budgeted at 1.2 billion rand, equivalent to 900 million in 1997 money. Boschkoppie will employ some 4,000.

At the same time, Amplats said it was budgeting 350 million rand (290 million in 1997 terms) for expanding the Potgietersrust Platinums (PP Rust) concentrator, lifting capacity from 250,000 tonnes per month to 375,000.

The increased capacity, expected to become available in early 1999, will be used to process the existing stockpile of low grade ore and the output of low grade ore from ongoing operations. No revision to current mining plans is necessary as no additonal tonnes will be mined.
